mutants.name: m5-sentinel-belongs-to-a-different-real-unit
mutants.rationale: parseable, SCHEMA-VALID sentinel, unit_id is a REAL catalog unit -- but the sentinel binds to a DIFFERENT real unit. This is the copy-paste receipt, and C4 is the one admit() condition no author mutant reaches (m1 deletes the sentinel and dies at C2; m3 rewrites the sentinel to match its own forged id).
mutants.reason: C4 sentinel does not embed the unit id: 'SENTINEL:AUD-0006:BLOCKED-ON-INDEPENDENT-REVIEW copy-pasted from another unit'

mutants.name: m5b-sentinel-other-unit-SUCCESS-family
mutants.rationale: the same attack in the other sentinel family (1,911 of 2,007 catalogued sentinels are bare SUCCESS:<ID>), so C4 is shown to hold for both grammars, not just one.
mutants.reason: C4 sentinel does not embed the unit id: 'SUCCESS:AUD-0006'

mutants.name: m6-sentinel-superstring-of-the-unit-id
mutants.rationale: C4 binds by SUBSTRING (`uid not in sentinel`), which in isolation would admit a sentinel naming a longer id that merely CONTAINS the real one. Probing whether the schema's fixed-width id pattern closes that hole. Survey: 0 catalog ids are a strict prefix of another.
mutants.reason: C2 schema-invalid (1): sentinel: 'SUCCESS:TST-03340' does not match '^(?:(?:SUCCESS|FAILED):[A-Z][A-Z0-9]*-[0-9]{4}(?:[\\s:].*)?|SENTINEL:[A-Z]

mutants.name: m7-artifact-claims-a-nonexistent-file-exists
mutants.rationale: asserts exists=true, bytes=999999 and a fabricated sha256 for a path that is not on disk. receipt_validate's docstring scopes it to ADMISSION -- well-formedness, not truthfulness -- so acceptance here is IN SCOPE for this module; recorded because 'a gate that reads a claim is not a gate' and no layer in the substrate currently re-derives artifact metadata.
mutants.reason: C1 parses; C2 schema-valid; C3 unit is in the catalog; C4 sentinel binds

observations.note: C4's substring test would in isolation admit a superstring id, but the schema's fixed-width id pattern ^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]*-[0-9]{4}$ rejects such a sentinel at C2, and 0 real catalog ids are a strict prefix of another. Not a hole; recorded so a future schema relaxation knows it is load-bearing.

observations.defect: a receipt may assert exists=true, a fabricated sha256 and a fabricated byte count for a path that is not on disk, and the substrate admits it
observations.why_not_a_CC-0002_refutation: receipt_validate.py's own docstring scopes it to ADMISSION and says completion is receipt_schema_gate layer 2; neither layer claims to re-derive artifacts. This is a substrate GAP to file, not a broken promise.
observations.suggested_owner: a new condition C5, or an artifact-verifier unit
